newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby vows fight for Alameda Cty, Calif., bonds.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby vows fight for Alameda Cty, Calif., bonds.

text.p: Municipal finance banker Calvin Grigsby, head of Grigsby & Associates, has vowed to fight to maintain his Alameda County, Calif., bond business, according to a published report Wednesday.

Contra Costa Times newspaper reported that Grigsby came to the county administrative offices on Tuesday to make his case to the Board of Supervisors to remain lead underwriter for a $293 million bond sale.
The county supervisors delayed any decision for two weeks, the newspaper reported.
"I won the deal, fair and square, on a competitive-bid basis," Grigsby told the Contra Costa Times.
Grigsby acknowledged that his San Francisco-based firm had undergone a massive shakeup, but said Grigsby & Associates was now recapitalized and was stable.
"I think the firm is stabilized now," Grigsby said. "I've been back to work for a month and a half and have talked to all the institutional buyers and we're comfortable."

Formerly known as Grigsby Brandford & Co, Grigsby's firm has undergone a dramatic shake-up since September, when Grigsby, the firm's founder and long-time chairman, abruptly announced his resignation.
After he left, it was disclosed that authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County, Fla. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
Several weeks after he left, Grigsby rejoined his firm, renaming it Grigsby & Associates.
The controversy surrounding Grigsby has taken a toll on his bond business across the country and in Alameda County.
In October, Grigsby was removed as a remarketing agent for commercial paper issued to renovate two Alameda County sports facilities.

In Alameda County on Tuesday, Grigsby said that he felt confident his company was capable of overseeing the $293 million debt sale to finance the county's employee pension fund, the Contra Costa Times reported.

But in a recent report to county supervisors, the county's administrator said that financial advisers believe the "market's perception of recent events involving Grigsby Brandford & Co could adversely impact the marketing of the county's bonds."
County administrators are recommending that Grigsby be bumped from the lead position and replaced by either of two co-senior underwriters.
